title: Normal energy and the actual glancing error operators
reviewed_arguments: All 30 original obligations, all 30 displays, three complete solutions and the original estimate diagram are retained unchanged.
The scalar wave principal form, positive spatial matrix, boundary block hypothesis and all complex matrix lower terms are retained on both actual weak form domains.
Supported/restricted derivative actions, full boundary source antiduals and common compact supports are explicit, with all constants uniform in the family parameter only at fixed widths.
The homogeneous tangential defect vanishes at the compact glancing anchor. The mean-value argument gives a width-independent leading coefficient.
Actual self-adjoint realization and strict principal square roots retain every order-minus-one and residual term. Symbol seminorm growth is assigned to the lower constants.
Both factorization signs and the real two-sided pairing bound are checked. The half-order pair estimate controls lower terms without an ordinary smoothing claim.
Spatial coercivity uses the real scalar principal form, the modulus of the complex weak form and each lower-term modulus. No normal integration by parts or strong Neumann condition is imposed.
Boundary coefficient freezing keeps the exact Cg h/kappa term. Every variable-coefficient derivative stays in the tangential operator.
The exact nested-cutoff identity preserves multiplication order. The full order-one decomposition keeps its left normal x factor and both actual distribution actions.

Time normalization uses the actual right parametrix and then a left parametrix of that T. The lacunary cutoff has x_in/x_out=1-t in (1/2,2), giving the doubled output collar; all full lower errors remain.

The patched normal commutator includes every support-cutoff derivative. Composition with B has the exact zero-derivative and one-normal-derivative orders, and preserves individual nonpositive coefficient orders.
The shifted u/source tester orders are nu-3/2 and nu-1/2. The leading normal constant retains the doubled collar and both factors of two.
The full principal-symbol extension for RT-minus is an explicit hypothesis. Its norm factorization retains the order-minus-one remainder and exact negative parametrix correction.
The actual linear error uses the unsquared normal norm, giving sqrt(omega)/epsilon and then sqrt(delta/epsilon), plus the exact Young remainder.
All three exercise proofs, finite checks, original estimate diagram and complete primary source pages were reviewed; no finite computation substitutes for an analytic proof.
